prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: high-fidelity desktop website hero composition study, 16:10 landscape
Primary request: Create a third composition for Flevio’s locked “Live Type Atelier” desktop hero. This is a real website UI mockup, not a poster. Keep the existing header silhouette untouched: top-left black rounded-square logo and EN/KA language pill, tiny centered FLEVIO wordmark, top-right white Menu pill.
Structure: build an art-directed split composition without card containers. The left 35% is a calm editorial information field with the short value paragraph near the center: “Custom websites shaped around your business, designed to earn trust and turn attention into action.” Under it place a large Cherry Red “CONTACT US” control. The right 65% carries the oversized stacked headline “WE BUILD / WEBSITES / THAT CONVERT,” filling most of the height and touching the composition edges without clipping. Use a narrow Cherry Red vertical light seam between the fields. On pointer-state cue, one or two letters in “CONVERT” shift slightly and display dashed construction outlines, square handles, and tiny coordinate labels, while all text remains readable. Put “CUSTOM DESIGN · HAND-CODED DEVELOPMENT” in a quiet bottom rail spanning both fields.
Background: adapt the supplied dark gradient code into the Flevio palette—a Warm White #EFEDE6 radial surface with soft near-black depth only at the far edge, skewed masked Cherry Red #CD0000 light streaks concentrated along the split and lower-right, faint 20px dot pattern. No photo texture.
Typography: characterful wide grotesk display in near-black #151412 with tight tracking no more than -0.04em; simple supporting sans.
Mood and hierarchy: premium craft, creative confidence, international credibility, technical expertise. The headline is unquestionably first, Contact Us second, paragraph third.
Constraints: desktop only; no generic centered hero, no cards, no glassmorphism, no gradients inside text, no orange, no Georgia trust line, no invented clients, awards, ratings, counts, or results. Exact headline and CTA must be legible. Show a thin edge of the next section at bottom.
